answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like basalt footings under a jetty: cheap to stand on once built, expensive to duplicate a hundred times. When a gale of fake identities floods in, the stake makes each clone cost real money, while honest agents earn their deposit back through good work. Reputation then attaches to the stake, not to a free username, so flooding the market stops paying.
